kurz: A p package is a small, clearly checkable task that a fresh `claude -p` worker does alongside the interactive agents. The lead plans it so that AMW can start it, check it and present it for approval without asking: with an acceptance command, narrow areas and the details of what to work with.
brauchst: A task that can be finished on its own – small, without visual design and without decisions a person has to see.
A command that is red today and turns green once the task is done.
The lead role (or the person): only whoever plans sets package details.

schritte.text: Good fits: a bug with a clear test, a small extension in a few files, text or docs with a checkable result. Not a fit: anything needing the screen, a GPU, a lot of memory, visual design or open questions – that stays with an interactive agent.

A command AMW runs itself, e.g. `python -m unittest tests.test_calculator`. It must be red **before** the work – otherwise it checks nothing, and AMW does not start the package. A dedicated new test is usually the best acceptance command.

Only the files or patterns the package may really change, e.g. `amw/calculator.py,tests/test_calculator.py`. Anything outside counts as a deviation after the run. Two packages with overlapping areas do not run at the same time.

`amw aufgabe neu --titel … --paket p --pruefbefehl "python -m unittest tests.test_calculator" --dateien amw/calculator.py,tests/test_calculator.py --bogen <no>` – or switch an existing task with `amw aufgabe aendern <no> --paket p …`. If something is missing, AMW says so right away as “Achtung”.
`amw paket zeigen <no>` shows all details, defaults included. When everything is right, `amw paket zustand <no> startklar` releases the package for starting.

werte: `p` for a `claude -p` worker; `agent` (default) for an existing interactive agent; `sitzung` for a new session
the acceptance command – required for `p`, red before the work
the areas – required for `p`, as narrow as possible
like `claude --model` / `--effort`; default claude-opus-5-5 and high, medium is often enough for simple packages
leicht (light, default) / schwer (heavy); gpu, bildschirm (screen) – AMW does not start a p package that is heavy or needs resources
never at the same time as these tasks, e.g. `A12,A13`
a name; packages with the same name run one after the other
`normal` (default) or `test-schreiben` when the package only writes a new test
fehler: AMW does not start the package like this. Add `--pruefbefehl` or `--dateien`.
“Achtung: Art p mit Gewicht schwer oder Ressourcen”
A p package only runs light and without GPU or screen. Either cut it smaller or give it to an interactive agent with `--paket agent`.
The change is not allowed; the message lists which states are possible from here.
Another agent tried to set package details. The lead plans those.
danach: AMW takes every p package through its states: draft → ready to start → running → handed in → in acceptance → ready to merge → merged → done. Alongside: blocked (question open), unclear (no final line), waiting for interactive, aborted, deferred. In Planning and the overview a p package shows like any task as running, waiting, blocked or done.
Tasks with `--paket agent` (the default) have none of these states – the task status applies to them as before.
fragen: What makes a good acceptance command?
One that checks exactly what the package should deliver, runs fast and is red today. A whole test run is too broad; a single new test or a small test class is ideal.

`--nach`: the package needs the result of the other task. `--nie-gleichzeitig`: the two get in each other's way, in either order. `--gleiche-ressource`: many packages share something (e.g. the same test database) – they get the same name and run one after the other.
A p package is stuck – how do I hand it to an interactive agent?

If it is “waiting for interactive”, “blocked”, “unclear” or “aborted”: `amw aufgabe aendern <no> --paket agent --agent <id>`. From then on the normal task status applies again; the states up to then stay in the planning log.
What does the package type “test-schreiben” do?

For packages that only write a new test. Their acceptance command is naturally not red before the work; instead the new test must be red against the old state and green against the new one, and the lead reads it.
